On reddit, when you delete a comment, your karma score isn't affected and the comment remains, but with your username replaced with [deleted].

On Voat, CCP scores are affected (which incentivizes people to delete their poorly scoring comments), and the comment completely disappears. That makes it easy to censor unpopular opinions by downvoating them until the OP deletes the comment.

Check this thread, for example. There are two comments that were downvoated to the bottom and deleted by the OP.
I honestly prefer the way reddit handles user-deleted comments.

On reddit, when you delete a comment [...] the comment remains, but with your username replaced with [deleted].

Wrong. When you delete a reddit comment, the comment is replaced with [deleted] for other users. When you delete your account, the comment remains and your username is removed.

That makes it easy to censor unpopular opinions by downvoating them until the OP deletes the comment.

reddit users also delete heavily downvoted comments in order to stop getting downvoted, so how does copying reddit's system alleviate this?

They filled the role of modern police in a similar if not the same capacity.

The first sheriff in America is believed to be Captain William Stone, appointed in 1634 for the Shire of Northampton in the colony of Virginia. The first elected sheriff was William Waters in 1652 in the same shire (shire was used in many of the colonies, before the word county replaced it.) [...] In 1776 Pennsylvania and New Jersey adopted the Office of Sheriff in their Constitution.

[Source]

And it doesn't say anywhere that there weren't others in the between span of 124 years. I haven't done the research on it but it's reasonable to assume if I did I might find other sheriffs departments which existed in the time before the 3rd amendment was put into place.
